help_text:
Multi-strategy knowledge-graph extraction (Simple / SchemaJson / ToolCall), ported from the Python graph.kg_extractor

Usage: kg-extract [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  describe   Print the kg.provider/v1 manifest: provider identity, capabilities with input_schema / side_effects / output, and per-capability cli_spec
  available  Probe backend/feature availability (read-only: env vars, PATH, compiled features; never a network call). The exit code is always 0; misses are reported inside the JSON
  invoke     Invoke one capability with a JSON request and print exactly one kg.execution/v1 envelope on stdout (logs go to stderr). Errors set status=error with a machine-readable code and exit non-zero
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -c, --config <CONFIG>
          Config file path, or an inline JSON object (a value starting with '{'). Defaults to ~/.kg-extract/config.json when present

  -e, --engine <ENGINE>
          Extraction engine

          Possible values:
          - simple
          - schema-json
          - toolcall
          - agentic:     Experimental: whole document through one sandboxed, multi-turn SDK session (slices fed as turns; agent can grep/read the doc for context)
          
          [default: simple]

  -f, --file <FILE>
          Input file (use '-' or omit for stdin)

  -F, --input-format <INPUT_FORMAT>
          Input format: plain `text` (default), or chonkie `chunks` (JSON/JSONL, e.g. from `chonkie --jsonl`) consumed as-is — the chunking engines skip their internal re-chunking and extract per given chunk

          Possible values:
          - text:   Plain text — segmented internally per --chunker
          - chunks: Pre-chunked chonkie output (JSON array or JSONL, e.g. `chonkie --jsonl`). The chunking engines (simple / agentic) use the chunks AS-IS instead of re-chunking; the single-shot engines (schema-json / toolcall) join them
          
          [default: text]

  -m, --model <MODEL>
          Model name (overrides the engine default)

  -b, --backend <BACKEND>
          Completion backend

          Possible values:
          - llms:  In-process `llms` crate (requires the `llms-backend` feature)
          - agent: Agent CLI driven through the `claude-agent-sdk-rs` stream-json protocol (minimaxcc / glmcc / mimocc), or pi-rs's `pi-agent`. Provider chosen by --agent
          - mock:  Deterministic mock (reads a canned response from --mock-response)
          
          [default: llms]

      --agent <AGENT>
          Agent CLI to use when --backend agent: minimaxcc / glmcc / mimocc / pi-agent (default minimaxcc)
          
          [default: minimaxcc]

  -k, --chunker <CHUNKER>
          Chunking strategy
          
          [default: recursive]
          [possible values: char, recursive, token]

      --schema-mode <SCHEMA_MODE>
          Schema mode for the schema-driven engines (schema-json / toolcall): `open` (no predefined types, default) / `fixed` (use only the schema) / `evolving` (seed schema, allow new types). `fixed` and `evolving` require --schema
          
          [default: open]
          [possible values: open, fixed, evolving]

      --schema <SCHEMA>
          Schema JSON file (entity/relation/attribute types) for schema-json / toolcall. Required for --schema-mode fixed|evolving; ignored by --schema-mode open

      --preset <PRESET>
          Built-in extraction preset (rich template) by name, e.g. `general/concept_graph`, `finance/event_timeline`, or a bare `graph` (resolved under `general/`). Routes through the schema-json engine and drives the prompt from the preset's guideline + fields. See --list-presets

      --preset-file <PRESET_FILE>
          Path to your own template YAML (same format as the built-in presets). Takes precedence over --preset

      --lang <LANG>
          Language to render the preset/template in (e.g. `zh`, `en`). Defaults to the template's first declared language

      --list-presets
          List the bundled presets (key + description) and exit

      --describe
          Describe CLI capabilities and output contracts, then exit

      --dry-run
          Print the resolved extraction plan without reading input or calling a backend

      --max-rounds <MAX_ROUNDS>
          Tool-call engine: max tool-calling rounds (1 = single-round collection)
          
          [default: 1]

      --merge-strategy <MERGE_STRATEGY>
          How duplicate entities are combined when deduping: keep-existing (default) / keep-incoming / field-union / llm (LLM-synthesised description)
          
          [default: keep-existing]
          [possible values: keep-existing, keep-incoming, field-union, llm]

      --coref
          Entity coreference: also merge surface variants of the same name (case, punctuation, corporate suffixes, near-identical spellings) across chunks, not just exact-label duplicates. Off by default

      --canonical-direction
          Canonical predicate direction: flip triples on the non-canonical member of an inverse pair (endpoints swapped, predicate → inverse) at the merge stage, so direction variants like (A, USES, B) vs (B, IS_USED_BY, A) dedup to one edge. Off by default

      --max-concurrency <MAX_CONCURRENCY>
          Max concurrent backend calls: per-chunk extraction (Simple engine) and per-community summary calls (--community-summaries). 1 = sequential
          
          [default: 8]

      --relation-gleaning <RELATION_GLEANING>
          Simple engine: targeted relation-gleaning rounds run after entity gleaning. Each round re-questions orphan entities (no relationship) to recover their edges. 0 (default) keeps the original behaviour
          
          [default: 0]

      --mock-response <MOCK_RESPONSE>
          Canned response for --backend mock

      --mock-tool-calls <MOCK_TOOL_CALLS>
          Scripted tool calls for --backend mock with --engine toolcall. Accepts inline JSON or a JSON file path. Shape: `[{"name": "...", "arguments": {...}}]` for one round, or `[[...], [...]]` for many rounds

      --community-summaries
          GraphRAG-style community summaries: with `-o communities` / `-o communities-hierarchy`, call the backend once per community (per level, in hierarchy mode) to generate a `{name, summary}` report merged into the community JSON. Calls run with bounded concurrency (--max-concurrency); the output is deterministic regardless of completion order. A failed community degrades to null name/summary with a stderr warning; the run does not fail

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - json
          - jsonl
          - kg-protocol
          - node-link
          - ladybug-import
          - communities:           Community detection over the extracted graph (label propagation, multiplicity-weighted). Requires building with `--features community`
          - communities-hierarchy: Hierarchical Leiden community levels (coarse → fine, per-level quality score). Requires building with `--features community-leiden`
          - mermaid
          - stats
          
          [default: json]

      --json
          Machine-readable JSON for --describe and --dry-run only

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Source: ~/projects/kg/kg-extract
source: kg-extract --help (user-facing flag enumeration of the frozen binary)
